  [
   {
    "title": "transfer's auths argument can move a callee-local authority into the caller: a dead local stays readable and writable after exitFrame, and the reject verdicts of cases 17 and 10 can be bypassed",
    "severity": "blocking",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:456 (TransferPre auths clause), :439 (transferEff rewrites frame), :241/:604 (CanReadLeaf/canWrite3 do not check Usable), :1794 (dependent_cannot_escape_frame), cases 10/17 at :2184-2191 and :2243-2245",
    "cause": "formalization error",
    "evidence": "The only conditions on `b ∈ auths` are `s.Active b ∧ s.frameOf b = placeFrame s.P src`. transferEff then rewrites b's holding frame to the destination's frame. As a result, the root authority of any callee local can be moved to the caller by moving an unrelated value. Both exitFrame and NoEscape decide 'local' by the mutable `frame` field, so neither sees the escape.\n\nEvery step below is checked with `decide` (scratch files review/Escape.lean and review/Case10.lean):\n\n(1) Dead local read. Caller place 0; callee places 1 (local L) and 2 (W).\n`e3 := transferEff e2 2 0 [1]`: `TransferStep K0 2 0 [1] e2 (.ok e3)`, `ExitStep e3 (.ok e4)`, `¬ e4.Usable 1`, then `Read3Step 1 [1] e4 (.ok e4)` and `Write3Step 1 [1] e4 (.ok _)` both succeed.\n\n(2) Case 17 bypassed. `TransferStep K0 3 0 [] h2 .reject` is the module's verdict. But after `TransferStep K0 4 1 [2] h2 (.ok h3)`, a carrier move that re-homes the root authority 2 of local L, the same `TransferStep K0 3 0 [] h3` is `ok`. `ExitStep h4` is then `ok` and leaves `(exitEff h4).D 0 = [2] ∧ ¬ (exitEff h4).Usable 2`.\n\n(3) Case 10 bypassed in one step. `TransferStep K0 2 0 [1, 3] (dependEff c10b 2 3) (.ok d1)` and `ExitStep d1 (.ok _)` both succeed, where the module has `ExitStep c10c .reject`.\n\nSpec, MM-03.3.1: « Un emplacement local ne peut être utilisé après la sortie de son cadre, sauf si une valeur transférable a été légalement déplacée » and « Un accès temporaire ne peut être prolongé simplement en le stockant dans un cadre plus ancien ». O4: « Une autorité dont l'origine est strictement locale au cadre appelé ne peut pas être rendue persistante dans l'appelant par cette seule opération ».\n\n`dependent_cannot_escape_frame` and `exitFrame_releases_all` still hold in these escaped states, because 'held by f' was rewritten. The verdicts of cases 10 and 17 depend on the tests choosing `auths = []`. Report (c) 12 and (e) 4 discuss `auths` but never mention this consequence.",
    "fix": "Constrain auths so that a transfer cannot make a callee-local authority persistent in an older frame (O4, last paragraph), or add usability of the leaf's place to CanReadLeaf/canWrite3 (MM-03.3.1). Since which authorities a value contains is open ((e) 4), report this as a consequence in (c)/(e) and re-check cases 10 and 17 against non-empty auths."
   },
   {
    "title": "The arena test contract KA violates ArenaResetContract; under KA, reset is accepted while a usable dependent exists",
    "severity": "major",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:2074 (KA), :2037 (ArenaResetContract), :1916 (ResetPre), cases 7/16 at :2147-2150 and :2236-2238; report (g) rows 7 and 16",
    "cause": "formalization error",
    "evidence": "KA.Invalidates r x := x = r only invalidates the anchor itself. ArenaResetContract also requires Invalidates for every authority derived from the anchor.\n\nScratch file review/Reset.lean, all checked with `decide`, on the case-16 state right after issue (callee frame still on the stack):\n- `c16c.1.D 5 = [4] ∧ c16c.1.Usable 5`. The block value depends on the `let` parameter authority 4, which is derived from anchor 0.\n- `ReleaseStep 5 c16c.1 (.ok r1)`.\n- `ResetStep KA c16c.2 r1 (.ok (resetEff r1 c16c.2))`: the reset is accepted.\n- `¬ ArenaResetContract KA r1 ar16`.\n\nThe same failure holds on the module's own state: `¬ ArenaResetContract KA c16e ar16`. Spec §11 case 7 expects `arena.reset()` with a still-usable dependent to be « Rejet ». Report (g) classifies cases 7 and 16 as « abstraction (Arena, KA) ». The module's case 7 only tests a dependent anchored directly on the anchor. `arena_reset_rejects_live_dependents_underInv` never applies to the test contract.\n\nAlso, K is fixed for the run and Invalidates cannot see `s.ancs`. A K that satisfies ArenaResetContract in every state would need `Invalidates anchor x` for every future authority id, which over-rejects unrelated dependents.",
    "fix": "Instantiate the arena cases with a K that satisfies ArenaResetContract on the states used, or report the gap. Note in (e) that the obligation depends on the state while K does not."
   },
   {
    "title": "arena_reset_rejects_live_dependents only restates ResetPre, and the report does not say so",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:2043-2048 (also arena_reset_rejects_live_issued :2031-2033, resetEff :1926); report (a)/(h)",
    "cause": "report error",
    "evidence": "The proof is `.reject fun h => h.2 q ?_ hq x hx (hk x hxa)`, which is clause 2 of ResetPre, instantiated through the hypothesis. `resetEff` leaves S3 unchanged (`(s, {ar with ...})`), so no I3-related state change is validated. Without the K hypothesis, a reset with a live dependent passes: `ResetStep K0 c16c.2 (releaseEff c16e 5) (.ok _)` is checked in review/Cases.lean, while `(exitEff c8e)`-style re-anchoring has left place 4 depending on anchor 0.\n\nSpec §10: « Une preuve qui réénonce directement une précondition comme conclusion ne constitue pas, à elle seule, une validation suffisante du mécanisme ». The report lists this theorem as the §10 property with no such caveat. It already gives one for O1.4/canWrite3 in (e) 10.",
    "fix": "State in the report (d)/(h) that both arena reset theorems are precondition restatements and that reset has no effect on S3."
   },
   {
    "title": "IssuePre has no non-escape check (MM-03.3.6): issue can place a value anchored on a callee-local arena into a caller place",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:1884-1891 (IssuePre), :1900-1906 (issueEff anchors dst on via); report (c) 13",
    "cause": "formalization error",
    "evidence": "Scratch file review/Issue.lean, checked with `decide`. Caller place 0; callee arena with metadata place 1 (root anchor 1) and storage place 2.\n- `IssueStep KA ai 1 [3] 0 i0 (.ok _)` succeeds, with `D 0 = [1]`: the anchor is a root local to the callee.\n- The same installation by `DependStep 0 1 i0` is `.reject`, because of NoEscape.\n- The escape is only caught later: `ExitStep (issueEff i0 ai 1 [3] 0).1 .reject`. With the auths bypass from the first finding, it is not caught at all.\n\nSpec, MM-03.3.6: « Une valeur dépendante ne peut être installée dans une destination dont le cadre survivrait à celui d'une ancre locale dont elle dépend ». Report (c) 13 says NoEscape is applied at O4.6 and O5.5 and does not mention issue.",
    "fix": "Add NoEscape for `via` and `placeFrame dst` to IssuePre, or list this choice in (c)/(e)."

    "title": "Docstring defects: a cited theorem does not exist, and some spec-encoding declarations have no docstring",
    "severity": "minor",
    "location": "formal/Ern/MM03.lean:338 (DerivePre), :812-816 (Mode.le_refl / effective_le), :1933 and :1937 (issue_ok_iff, reset_ok_iff)",
    "cause": "formalization error",
    "evidence": "- The DerivePre docstring justifies omitting O1.5 by « derive ne désactive aucune autorité (`derive_keeps_active`) ». `grep derive_keeps_active` matches only that docstring; no such theorem exists.\n- The docstring « Le mode effectif n'excède pas le mode de l'autorité (MM-03.3.5) » is attached to `Mode.le_refl` at line 813. `effective_le`, which states that property and which report (a) lists under MM-03.3.5, has no docstring.\n- `issue_ok_iff` and `reset_ok_iff` are listed under §6 in report (a) but have no docstring, while every other `*_ok_iff` cites its clause. AGENTS.md: « Every definition or theorem that encodes a spec rule cites the rule's location in its docstring ».",
    "fix": "Prove or remove the `derive_keeps_active` reference, move the MM-03.3.5 docstring onto effective_le, and add clause-citing docstrings to issue_ok_iff and reset_ok_iff."
   }

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

- Do not edit `specs/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `formal/DESIGN.md` unless the task says so.

## Lean

- The Lake project is in `formal/`. `formal/DESIGN.md` governs how to formalize, never what the semantics is. Propose design decisions it does not settle in your report; never take them silently.
- Every definition or theorem that encodes a spec rule cites the rule's location in its docstring.
- A definition says what its rule says. Never make a definition more permissive, add an unjustified hypothesis or narrow a theorem's domain to obtain a proof.
- Never change a theorem statement, or a definition it depends on, to make a proof go through. If stuck, stop and report the goal state.
- Never use `sorry`, `admit`, `axiom` or `native_decide`.

## Report

Spec passages implemented (by location), what changed, what is unproven or open, spec problems found.

## Review (Codex)

Adversarial and read-only. For each change, check:

- It says exactly what the spec says: not stronger, not weaker. Read definitions, hypotheses and quantifiers, not only proofs. A theorem that holds because a definition is too permissive or its hypotheses are unsatisfiable is blocking.
- Each formalized rule cites its spec location.
- No theorem statement or dependency was changed without the task allowing it.
- No interpretation was chosen silently where the spec is unclear.
- Nothing outside the task was added.

When a milestone is declared complete, compare the rules in its announced scope with the spec locations cited in `formal/`, and list every rule left without a definition or theorem.

Every finding needs evidence: a spec quote, a counterexample or command output. No evidence, no finding. Never ask for additions beyond the task.

Output: verdict (block / changes / ok), then each finding with severity, location, cause (formalization error, missing coverage or spec defect) and evidence.
